tokenConvention: tokens = the word's written base letters in reading order, each with its own marks; a doubled letter (with shadda) is ONE token.
'ـ' separates words in a phrase test and is never stressed.
Hamzat al-waṣl is written 'ا', and the article lām is a separate token ('ل' or 'لْ').
Some tests show only the relevant fragment of a phrase (e.g. 'شَّ مْ سَ ـ سِ ...'); match from the first token, not the full word.
Tokens list the letters a student sees; the engine works on pronounced units. Map engine output to tokens by walking base letters (marks stripped) in order.
When a highlighted token is a doubled letter, the stress belongs to its second (voweled) half; colour the whole glyph.
context: 'wasl' = joined reading, 'waqf' = pausing on the word, 'default' = joined reading and, for a single word, assume it is not the last word of an āya.
naturalStressNote: Expected sets include 'natural' stresses (a letter followed by sukūn), which the book counts as weak. The engine should emit them with level=weak and isNatural=true so the UI can hide them with a filter.

tests.source: part0.ch4 The Two Functions of Nabr

tests.source: part0.ch4 The Two Functions of Nabr

tests.reasonEn: Before the final shadda: "more bitter".

tests.reasonEn: Bāʾ after the sukūn; hamza naturally.

tests.reasonEn: A two-letter word, stressed both ways.

tests.source: part1.ch5 Separating and Joining Two Words

tests.source: part1.ch5 Separating and Joining Two Words

tests.reasonEn: One-letter preposition + pronoun.

tests.reasonEn: The added wāw changes nothing.

tests.reasonEn: Mother of pronouns: hāʾ, not lām.
tests.reasonAr: أمّ الضمائر: الهاء لا اللام.

tests.reasonEn: Like *-hunna*: the following letter is doubled.

tests.reasonEn: Mīm naturally; hāʾ after the sukūn.

tests.reasonEn: Lām is added; *qad* is two letters.

tests.reasonEn: The question hamza is added.

tests.reasonEn: Yāʾ, not bāʾ; stressing bāʾ is clipping.

tests.reasonEn: Ghayn, so the lām isn't heard as a root letter.

tests.reasonEn: "Their hearts hardened" (Ḥadīd 16). Stressing the fāʾ makes it "the egg hatched".

tests.reasonEn: One-letter preposition + pronoun (Rule 6).
tests.reasonAr: جارّ أحادي بعده ضمير.

tests.reasonEn: Mīm naturally; qāf before the 2nd sukūn and before the final shadda at a pause.

tests.reasonEn: One of the five relative-*mā* places (Special 1).

tests.reasonAr: الواو زائدة والدال أول الأصول، والثالث متحرك.

tests.reasonEn: Emphatic lām, not the preposition (Special 7).
